articles.title: All Relic Point Locations (Militech Data Terminals) - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty DLC unlocks a whole new Relic skill tree for V, but you’ll need to find Restricted Militech Data Terminals to earn
articles.body:
The Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty DLC unlocks a whole new Relic skill tree for V, but you’ll need to find Restricted Militech Data Terminals to earn skill points for it. The tree contains 15 new skills, and a simple level-up won’t do the trick, so we’re here to help you find all Relic Skill Point Locations in Dogtown.

Your new Netrunner friend, Songbird , will give you three Relic skill points for free when you meet her at the start of the Phantom Liberty story, and she’ll do the same again during the Birds With Broken Wings main mission. This means there are only nine Militech Data Terminals to find.

Looking for a particular Militech Data Terminal? Click the links below to jump to...

You’ll need to progress the Phantom Liberty story a bit to be able to freely roam around the new district, but this data terminal can be found before you gain access to the full Dogtown map. It’s at the north end of the Petrochem Stadium , behind a statue of three athletes. You’ll hear a pinging noise and see a flashing white light as you approach the terminal. Crouch under the shelving to reach it.

The next Militech Data Terminal is right next to the Kress Street fast travel point. You’ll find it directly underneath the abandoned apartment that V is using as a hideout. As soon as you exit the building for the first time, you should see the nearby Relic icon appear on the map since it’ll be directly below you.

This data terminal is directly south of the Dogtown main gate on the map, and if you create a marker in the location pictured below, you’ll find it on the second level of a crowded parking garage . You can see and hear the terminal from above, on the roof, through a grated ceiling.

This terminal is underneath a large building with Voodoo Boys graffiti on the front. It’s behind a barricade near the entrance to the building, down one set of stairs. The terminal should appear on your map as you approach the entrance to the seemingly abandoned building.

The Luxor High Wellness Spa fast travel point is right next to a Voodoo Boys hideout , which is where you’ll find this Militech Data Terminal. You’ll need to take down a bunch of Voodoo Boys gang members to find the terminal on the back wall inside the hideout.

This terminal is located right outside the Petrochem Stadium on the east side of Dogtown. It’s sitting next to an overpass across from the Heavy Hearts Club – the pyramid-shaped building where Mr. Hands does business.

This data terminal is near the Terra Cognita fast travel point on the far southwest side of Dogtown. It’s inside a Scavengers gang base, so you’ll need to fight your way to its location. The terminal is on the top floor of the base, inside a back room.

There’s a Barghest base entrance near the Kress Street fast travel point, and it’ll take you underground. This underground base houses a Militech Data Terminal, but it’s behind a door that requires 12 Technical Ability to open.

If you don’t have enough points, go to the spot shown in the screenshot below and drop down underneath the floor grating . You’ll find a ladder that brings you into the data terminal room from below.

We’ve circled both the terminal and the base’s entrance on the map below – the entrance is right next to the motorcycle icon on the map.

During the Lucretia My Reflection mission, you’ll be given the option to follow the power cables out of the Capitán Caliente restaurant. Follow them up to the roof of the Brainporium to find this Militech Data Terminal near the objective. The terminal is facing the back of The Heavy Hearts Club pyramid, and you’ll need to climb up a bit to reach it.

articles.title: Spider and the Fly Walkthrough - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This is the walkthrough of Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty's Spider and the Fly, the third mission in the expansion. You managed to get the NUSA president
articles.body:
This is the walkthrough of Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty 's Spider and the Fly, the third mission in the expansion. You managed to get the NUSA president out of immediate danger, but her safety is far from secure.

Use the links below to skip between major quest steps:

Hansen's men are honed in on getting rid of Myers, so get her out of the wreckage and regroup with Songbird as fast as you can.

After clearing the areas of the incoming attackers at the end of Hole in the Sky , return to Myers and escort her safely out of the wreckage.

Midway through, Myers will ask you to remove the subdermal tracker implanted in her neck - any option will work.

Do it in time before the scout drone sees you.

The next elevator will lead you to the restaurant—but it is not powered, so you'll need to override the generator to turn it back on.

The generator is located in the room adjacent to the left of the elevator, but unless you have Body Level 15 to force open the door, you'll need to go down the scaffolding outside of the hallway and enter the room from below.

There will be a drone out the restaurant windows hunting for you. You'll need to sabotage the access point so Songbird can distract it.

Use your minimap to indicate the Drone's location while you sneak your way to the access point:

The next room will contain several soldiers guarding the exit; you can go guns blazing or take them out individually.

The best path for the stealth option is to head right and take out the two on the highest platform.

Then, go down the stairs, crouch past the soldier by the vending machines, and kill the one inside the small room.

Get rid of the last soldier outside and circle the building to escape.

You can also use the BARGHEST car to get to the building on Elizabeth Kress Street quickly. However, using their vehicle won't camouflage you from the patrolling BARGHEST soldiers around Dogtown, but it will allow you to get to the next objective much faster.

Once you reach the parking lot, take the elevator up and talk to Myers inside the museum when prompted.

There are two doors on each side of the elevated platforms in the lobby that you can access with either Body Level 15 or Technical Ability Level 15 . Each room contains several items in various rarities.

You can't access these rooms once you get inside the exhibit room.

Be sure to explore this central room to grab ammo and other loot, as interacting with the elevator button will initiate the following combat sequence.

You'll need to fight off Hansen's soldiers to buy time for Songbird to take control of the Chimera in the middle of the room.

It's best to stay and fight the enemies near the elevator, as many of them will take cover on the second floor.

With the controlled Chimera, Songbird will eliminate the rest of the Barghest Soldiers before losing control of the mech.

The first boss fight of Phantom Liberty will put you against the same mech that helped you wipe out dozens of Hansen's men.

The Chimera fight is split into three phases:

Phase 1: The first phase requires you to focus on destroying the exposed bits of its armor. There are several around its legs and a few around its head.

Range builds can quickly shoot these exposed areas from the second-floor platforms for safety; just be wary of the missiles and especially the laser beam covering the entire boss arena.

For melee builds , it's best to go for the weak points on its legs, as they are easier to reach with your weapon.

If you have a Berserk or Sandevistan OS, dropping the boss to its second phase will be short work.

Phase 2: Once you drop the Chimera to around 70% health, the support and repair drones will spawn to aid the boss.

Focus on destroying the repair drones first and then the support drones. Getting rid of the former will immediately start the third phase.

Be careful of its laser beam attack. This move will cover the entire boss arena, but the Chimera will aim only at the ground floor or the second floor, never both simultaneously.

Phase 3: Chimera's third phase is relatively straightforward, as you can damage any part of its armor without resistance.

At around 5% health, it will unleash a cloud of toxic gas on the first floor; this move does a ton of damage, so you'll want to go up to the second-floor platform as that's the only way of dodging it.

Once the boss reaches 2%, you'll want to jump onto the Chimera and finish it by pressing the prompt - this animation changes based on whether you have Arm cyberware or not.

Before leaving the area, be sure to pick up the active Chimera core on the floor. You can later use this to craft one of four Tier 5 Iconic weapon mods.

Click the link below to continue to the next mission in Phantom Liberty :

articles.title: Lucretia My Reflection Walkthrough - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This is the walkthrough of Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty's Lucretia My Reflection, the fourth mission in the expansion. You survived the Chimera attack;
articles.body:
This is the walkthrough of Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty 's Lucretia My Reflection , the fourth mission in the expansion. You survived the Chimera attack; it's a shame that Songbird was the price to pay for it, though her demise is uncertain.

With Songbird MIA, your only route is to take Myers to the original rendezvous location. Use the links below to jump to key steps:

The museum's exit is hidden behind a shipment container close to the main staircase. The container should be highlighted when using your scanner—open it and lead Myers through the subway tunnels.

Johnny is finally free, but you still won't be able to reach Songbird.

Talking to him is optional, but you'll be able to get some extra information about what could be going on with her.

Lead Myers Out of the Tunnels - Go Left or Right

You'll find a forked path after pushing the minecart to clear the way. Going right will require you to shut off the steam pipe to get through—while going left will require you to go through a survey pipe blocked by a piece of machinery. Either way, both paths will lead you to an elevator you need to take.

Shutting off the steam pipe requires turning the valve hidden behind some scaffolding ; you'll need to climb it and drop below to access the valve.

To access the survey pipe, you only need to turn on the machinery right next to it.

Use the elevator to get to the 8th floor and access the apartments.

When you leave the elevator, scan the King of Pentacles Tarot Card Graffiti on the wall to your right.

In the room where you're supposed to meet Songbird, there will be a home-cooked generator you can kick-start to get the power back up.

After speaking with Johnny, you can find the battery needed to power the generator inside a broken drone in the living room with the exposed window.

Insert the battery into the case and fire up the generator to restore power to the apartment.

After the dialogue with Myers over Hansen's speech, some scavengers will come through the front door. You can choose to kill them outright or make a deal.

If you do the latter, you can talk to Jacob and Taylor separately to gain more information about their connection with Kurt Hansen.

Keeping them around is also helpful, as they'll give you valuable information on Hansen's airdrops and other notable things about Dogtown.

The following day, with no signs of Songbird, Myers wants to acquire the help of Solomon Reed , a sleeper agent who used to work for NUSA alongside Songbird. You'll need to be registered in the FIA database to remove any doubt when you meet Reed; choosing to take the oath or not will only create a different dialogue with Johnny and Reed later. There is no tangible impact for either option.

When you're ready, use the elevator to return to street level to continue the quest.

From here on out, you can continue the Phantom Liberty main storyline or freely explore Dogtown.

Mr. Hands will shortly call to notify you of your registration in the Dogtown member registry, allowing you to go in and out of the zone whenever you like.

Mr. Hands will also send you the Tanishi-400 for free.

Make your way to the Capitan Caliente restaurant to contact Reed.

The main entrance is locked but can be opened if you have Level 20 in either Body or Technical Ability . However, there are a couple of alternatives you can use to open the door.

The first alternative is to scan the power cable attached to the window to the right of the entrance and follow it to the fusebox.

From there, override the fusebox to open the door.

Another way to get inside is to push the garbage disposal to the left side of the restaurant and enter the hole in the wall behind it—this requires Body Level 15.

Use your scanner to reveal scratches on the floor in the hallway adjacent to the kitchen. Move the cabinet to the side and use the old telephone behind it.

Once you speak to Reed on the phone, head over to the meeting point by the basketball court. Sit down near the court and talk to Johnny about his military past; soon, Reed will come from behind you to quickly interrogate who you are.

Walk to Reed's car and speak with him on the way back to the apartment. Go up using the elevator and knock on the door to enter.

Depending on your earlier choice with Jacob and Taylor, they may or may not be there.

Speak to Myers and Reed in private; there are several choices you can make during the conversation, but there are two important dialogue moments here.

The first is when Reed asks you, "I don't know how much they're paying you, but you better ask yourself - is it worth it?" Your response here is crucial to continue the Phantom Liberty storyline.

Once Myers asks if you really want to walk away, you have one more chance to either continue the storyline or quit.

Note: Failing Lucretia My Reflection will lock you out of the rest of the Phantom Liberty Main Jobs.

You'll still be able to explore Dogtown and access some, but not all, of the district's side jobs, gigs, and other added bonuses.

Once you have finished speaking with those two, pick up the Iconic Hawk assault rifle by the computer and talk to Jacob and Taylor before exiting the building.

You can also wait for Reed and Myers to leave first.

If you haven't already done so, you can fix the Homemade Water Pump in the hallway to supply water to the apartment.

The mission will be complete after two in-game days when Reed gives you a call—you can explore Dogtown for some side jobs and gigs or skip time while you wait for the call.

Click the link below to continue to the next mission in Phantom Liberty :

articles.title: The Damned Walkthrough - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This is the walkthrough of Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty's The Damned, the fifth mission in the expansion. Without a clue of Songbird's location,
articles.body:
This is the walkthrough of Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty 's The Damned , the fifth mission in the expansion. Without a clue of Songbird's location, Reed suggests the help of a former colleague and ex-protege, Alex. In this guide, you'll find all the ways you can infiltrate the Voodoo Boys' hideout, either through sheer force or by finding the door code for the side entrance, as well as whether or not you can save Slider.

Go inside The Moth and sit by the bar; it doesn't matter what order of drink you choose. Reed will shortly ring your cellphone to provide more context about his relationship with Alex.

Once the bartender clears the bar, she will reveal herself as Alex. If you have at least Level 15 Reflex , you can disarm her here; otherwise, diffuse the situation before the dialogue option runs out.

Walk outside the bar and talk to Alex, brief her about the operation, and when you're done, head back inside and inform Reed that she's in.

After talking to Alex and Reed about Slider , go outside and talk to Johnny before leaving for Slider's hideout in Luxor High .

When walking into the building with Reed, you can choose to deal with The Voodoo Boys' guards head-on or find another entrance. However, if you have at least Body Level 15 , you can talk to the guards without immediately triggering a fight.

If you've completed The Voodoo Boys' associated main job, Transmission , with Placide and Brigitte and spared them at the end, you can choose the corresponding dialogue option, and the guards will let you enter with no problem.

If you haven't, you can choose to fight them by opting for the codeword option, or you can leave and find another way in.

The next room contains many enemies, but if you can find a way without hostility, you can safely loot some of the equipment there.

There is also a side entrance you can use that requires a door code. The door code is 230598 ; however, it can also be found by reading a Worker Memo at the top of the front scaffolding.

If you prefer to access the side entrance without the code, you can find the other door to the ventilation shaft by climbing the scaffolding to the right of the building's entrance.

Be wary of the first grating inside the shaft; it will open as soon as you set foot on it, causing you to fall to the room below you. You can scan it and then disarm the trapdoor.

Keep moving through the shaft until you get to the central hub room. The entrance to Slider's lair is downstairs; you'll need to disable the first two security cameras on the second floor before dropping down using the ladder.

Nearby: If you've completed the Gig Treating Symptoms and got the Storage Room Key, you will be able to open this private area on the top floor to find the Gris-Gris Iconic tech revolver inside a crate. The door to the storage room has a skeleton painted on it.

From there, either use any stealth Cyberware such as the Optical Camo or wait for the enemies to move away from the tunnel entrance before running there.

Once you're inside, the door will close, and they won't be able to follow you. Go inside the room and talk to Slider. He will ask you to link your Relic with him, revealing that Songbird was able to communicate by using the Blackwall .

There will be extra dialogue options if you have at least Level 15 Intelligence to dig deeper into the lore of the Blackwall.

Proceed with the conversation until you are prompted to confirm the data transfer with Slider. During the data transfer, you can briefly communicate with Songbird.

Due to the damage netrunners can sustain when connecting to the Blackwall, Slider will have taken too much damage to survive no matter what you do.

The damage Slider took from the data breach will spread to the central hub, causing the patrolling guards from before to die as well.

Several Voodoo Boys will enter the room to investigate what happened, and you must either fight them head-on or find a way to escape stealthily.

Once outside, follow Reed and speak to him about the plan to infiltrate Black Sapphire to finish the mission.

Click the link below to continue to the next mission in Phantom Liberty :

articles.title: How to Unlock Oogie Boogie - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Oogie Boogie is a sinister trickster who hails from the world of Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas. In Disney Dreamlight Valley, he joins as
articles.body:
Oogie Boogie is a sinister trickster who hails from the world of Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas. In Disney Dreamlight Valley , he joins as part of the Season of Scares update . However, Oogie Boogie has a somewhat unusual unlock process.

You need to complete a series of six Quests before the Boogeyman himself will join your Valley as a Villager. Beginning on September 23, 2026, one Quest will unlock each Wednesday for six weeks. At the end of the sixth Quest, Oogie Boogie will move in permanently!

If you start this Quest line once all Quests have released, you will only have to wait a short time (likely no more than a few hours) between Quests, as the next one will begin as soon as you get the next letter from Oogie Boogie in your Mailbox.

Important PSA for Unlocking Oogie Boogie

If you want to unlock Oogie Boogie in 2026, you MUST begin his first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , no later than November 4, 2026. Once you have begun the first Quest, the other five can be completed at any time once they have unlocked.

As long as you have STARTED A Halloween Invasion, you will be able to unlock Oogie Boogie, even if you finish up the Quest chain after November 4.

If you missed out on Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return to the Valley in October 2027 !

A Halloween Invasion is the first Quest needed to begin the process of unlocking Oogie Boogie. It is available from September 23, 2026 onward.

Enter the Strange Mirror inside Scrooge's Store to make your way to Oogie Boogie's Lair. There, you will need to help him repair his Lucky Wheel by playing the mini-game Whack-a-Pumpkin.

Once the Wheel is fixed, spinning it unleashes a Halloween Curse on the Valley! Clear out the Oogie Boogie Bugs from Mickey and Goofy's Houses, and remove the Sweet or Spooky Pumpkins from the Plaza or Peaceful Meadow. At the end of the Quest, give all the Fear Essence you collected performing these tasks to Oogie Boogie.

Quest Rewards: Lock Mask, Shock Mask, Barrel Mask, Oogie Boogie's Lair Skeletons

The Oogie Boogie Contract is the second Quest in the chain needed to unlock Oogie Boogie. It was released on September 30, 2026. You can begin this Quest after completing A Halloween Invasion and receiving a letter from Oogie Boogie in your mailbox.

This time, when you enter Oogie Boogie's Lair via the Strange Mirror and spin the Lucky Wheel, you become his minion! Use the Ghost Lantern he gives you to capture three Ghosties floating around his lair. Then, decorate your Valley using either Halloween furniture (if you choose to obey him) or Cute furniture (if you choose to defy him).

Next, release the Ghosties you caught in Mickey's House, Merlin's House, and Chez Remy. The Ghostie in Chez Remy is a bit of a trickster, so you'll need to put it back in the lantern! Finally, head back to Oogie Boogie's Lair and cook him some Snake and Spider Stew using the ingredients he has prepared for you.

Quest Rewards: Ghost Lantern, Ghost Well, U-Carve-It Pumpkin x 5

The Ghost in the Portrait is the third Quest in the chain required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager. It was released on October 7, 2026. After completing The Oogie Boogie Contract, you'll get another letter with a Lucky Wheel Ticket in your inbox.

Oogie Boogie admits that he's trapped Jack Skellington's dog Zero inside a Haunted Portrait, but he's not going to let you free him easily. Team up with Scrooge and Merlin to sabotage the Lucky Wheel - but that just makes Oogie Boogie mad, and he floods his Lair with portraits!

Find the real Haunted Portrait, then look for the five Zero Drawings hidden around Oogie Boogie's Lair to collect Zero Essence from each one. Use the Crafting Station to make Real Ghostly Paint Thinner, and apply it to your Royal Watering Can to free Zero from the portrait at last! Unfortunately, Oogie Boogie's pretty mad, and hints that he's cooking up something nasty for his next plan.

Quest Rewards: Zero ( Notable Companion )

Oogie Boogie is furious that you freed Zero, so he trapped several Villagers in his Lair. The threatening letter you receive in your Mailbox unlocks the fourth Quest, Rescue Mission , which initially released on October 14, 2026 .

Head through the mirror into the Lair to confront Oogie Boogie, who traps you in another game involving locating five pieces of artificial furniture . Then, enlist Zero's help to find Oogie Boogie's weakness: Extra-Strength Bug Spray.

Craft the Bug Spray using Dream Shards , Dandelions, and special items you can catch by fishing in the lava pool in Oogie Boogie's Lair. Hand off the Extra-Strength Bug Spray to Merlin and Scrooge to keep them safe from Oogie Boogie's tricks once and for all!

Quest Rewards: Decorative Oogie Boogie Bats

After fooling Oogie Boogie's plans multiple times, he's cooked up something extra-special for you in Let the Games Begin , which initially released on October 21, 2026.

Repair Oogie Boogie's Wheel into a Genuinely Lucky Wheel, then head to the Lair. Oogie Boogie has prepared four mini-games for you, and you'll need to collect an Oogie Boogie Tile from each one.

Spin the Genuinely Lucky Wheel, play a few rounds of Whack-a-Pumpkin, go fishing in the Lava Pool, and remove the five Hidden Smiles around the Lair. Then, use the Tiles you found to solve a Tile puzzle and reveal Oogie Boogie's frightening face. When you do, the Mirror Lair starts cracking, so make your escape to finish the Quest!

Oogie Boogie's Big Game is the final required Quest, which officially unlocks Oogie Boogie. It initially released on October 28, 2026, and began with a letter from Oogie Boogie inviting you back to his lair for a "final showdown."

This time, when you head into Oogie Boogie's Mirror Lair, he's set up a quiz board game for you. You must interact with each tile and correctly answer the question. There are 11 questions in total, and they are a mix of general Valley trivia, picture questions, and questions about Oogie Boogie.

While you must get them all right, you can stop and come back at any time, and Oogie Boogie will also give you as many guesses as you need for each question. The answers are listed below:

Once you have answered all questions correctly, head back to the Valley and place Oogie Boogie's House using Furniture Mode. Spend up to 10,000 Star Coins to build the House, then take a picture to officially welcome Oogie Boogie!

Quest Rewards: Oogie Boogie unlocked as a Villager

For more spooky fun in Disney Dreamlight Valley, check out...

Up Next: A Halloween Invasion Walkthrough

articles.title: All Visions and Locations in Final Fantasy Resonance - Final Fantasy Resonance Guide - IGN
articles.summary: As a mobile-turned-offline game, Final Fantasy Resonance ingeniously turned the gacha system from Brave Exvius into the Visions mechanic. Visions work as a
articles.body:
As a mobile-turned-offline game, Final Fantasy Resonance ingeniously turned the gacha system from Brave Exvius into the Visions mechanic. Visions work as a type of Job system, and equipping them on characters allows them to learn new spells and abilities, as well as improve their overall attributes. You can find 26 Visions in Final Fantasy Resonance , and we have compiled all of their locations in this guide, separated by chapter.

All Vision Locations in Final Fantasy Resonance

This guide is written as a walkthrough, so you can follow it from the start of your journey to ensure you never miss a Vision and can pick them up at the earliest possible opportunity.

There are 5 Visions to collect in Chapter 1.

These two are automatically acquired via the Main Story and function as the feature's tutorial.

This Visions is pretty hard to miss since it's marked on your map, but in case you did, it's found in a Sanctum of Light just north of Kol.

Once your goal changes to visit Felicitas and you get a Chocobo, you can ignore the main story path and, after crossing the bridge south of Kol, head to the west side of the map.

You'll eventually find Grandport Harbor. To the north of the harbor is the Siren's Cave, and to the east is a desert and the Wanderer's Cave. Cross the desert, circling around to the north side until you reach a beach on the west side. You'll find a Sanctum of Light there, housing Cloud.

The main story will take you to the Town of Felicitas and then to a nearby cave. Before proceeding, go all the way south in this region until you reach a peninsula. At the edge of this peninsula is the Sanctum of Terra, containing the descendant of Espers.

You can find 3 new Visions in Chapter 2.

After crossing Mt. Thunderclap, you'll be on your merry way to Dwarven Forge. After two bridges, the Sanctum will be to the west of a sign.

The Sanctum with Noctis is west of the Mobliz Shipyard entrance, pretty hard to miss.

You can get the Onion Knight as soon as the main objective asks you to go to the Mobliz Shipyard. Instead of going to the shipyard, go east to find the Wind Shrine. From the shrine, go south until you walk under three bridges and reach an intersection leading further south or east.

Take the east lane, keep going, then go west when you reach another crossroad amid the mountains to return to Mt. Gagazet. Inside Mt. Gagazet, exit it through the southwestern exit to return to the World Map. The Sanctum lies west of this area.

There are 3 Visions waiting for you in Chapter 3.

At the start of Chapter 3, you'll regain control on a shore. Go immediately northwest to find this Sanctum.

Starting at Olderion's position on the world map, go all the way west, crossing some bridges, a gorgeous waterfall, and the mysterious Secluded Dwelling, ultimately reaching the Sanctum of the protagonist from the best Final Fantasy.

From Olderion, go east until you encounter a sign. If you continue east and go up the slope, you'll reach the Water Cave. Instead, stay on the ground level and keep going east until the path turns north. Go all the way up to find the Sanctum of Squall.

The nexus between world will grant you 3 new Visions.

After you drop from the train, run east, past Mozul Station, until you reach the Sanctum of Shantotto.

Once in Zoldaad, return to the world map and keep going east to find this Sanctum midway along the path. It's also close to the Rebel Hideout, to the west of its world map location.

From Chapter 5 on, we have an airship to call ours. This dramatically expands our exploration scope. We'll also start earning Visions not only from Sanctums, but from sub quests as well. To keep this guide in order, we will tackle objectives by their in-game recommended level, while still prioritizing side content over the main story.

Once Chapter 5 starts, go to Zoldaad's Residential District and talk to the NPC to start the subquest The Call from Beyond. Now fast travel to either the Weapons Factory or Y'shtola's Sanctum, then go to the nearby subquest marker. You'll be transported to a phantom train.

All you have to do is talk with the NPCs. When prompted, answer "General Wilhelm's men," "Exposing Lazarov," and then "The remorse of the soldiers." Don't worry if you get any wrong, since the subquest will continue either way. Eventually, you'll fight a fairly easy monster that's weak to Light and Ice. Upon victory, you'll get a Magicite and Camille as a Vision.

Must complete The Call from Beyond sub quest first.

Travel to Zoldaad's castle plaza and talk to Ozetta to accept the O General! My General! sub quest. You need to examine two camps, one near the Sanctum of Shantotto and another south of the Weapons Factory, reachable only by air. Then, return to the Castle Plaza and talk to Ozetta.

Your next destination is the Weapons Factory. Once inside, go north from the save point and interact with the marker. Back in Zoldaad, talk to Foxie inside the inn to complete the sub quest and earn Wilhelm Vision.

The Sanctum is southwest of the Town of Mitra, on a patch of land reachable via airship.

Backtrack a little bit and go to Dilmagia, the Machinopolis. Upon entering, accept the sub quest Forger of Wills from a NPC near the entrance. Talk to Aileen in the shipyard, then gather some information about her in Dilmagia, the Rebel Hideout, and the Village of Kol. Return to Dilmagia's shipyard and talk to Aileen again. She'll ask you three questions. Respond with the following:

Aileen will then join your party (as a Vision).

Go east of Mysidia, past the Tower of Mysidia and Victoria's Shrine, to find the Sanctum of Vaan. Time to rake in some Gil.

South of Mysidia, you'll come across the Nameless Ruins. Take the east path from the ruins, and you'll soon find the Sanctum.

Once you deliver the potions to the Village of Sunioo, the sub quest Victoria Revivified will be available on Mysidia. Go to the city, teleport to the storefront, and talk to the mage Victoria. Next, go to the Potion Factory and watch the chaotic cutscene.

Back to the world map, your destination now is Victoria's Shrine, west of Mysidia, near the Sanctum of Vaan. After talking to one more Victoria, board your airship and fly to an island northeast of Mysidia to defeat some monsters. It's three level 35 black lizards. They're weak to Ice and can petrify your members. More annoyingly, they cast Graviga, and if two of them spam the magic, it's a tad scary. Still a pretty manageable battle, overall.

With victory in hand, go to the central pool area in Mysidia and sprinkle the powder to complete the quest, earning Victoria as a Vision and another Magicite.

Must complete Token Legacy sub quest first.

The trigger for Token Legacy is a bit mysterious. The sub quest automatically begins after sleeping at a random inn - except the Airship. The earliest it triggered for us was after delivering the potions to the Village of Sunioo. Once it starts, just follow the markers, and that's it.

After you complete the Token Legacy, a new sub quest will appear on the bulletin board in Zoldaad, the Imperial Capital. Interact with the board to start Errand's End. You only need to do a bit of legwork.

First, go to Castle Plaza and enter the castle to talk to Shera. Next, travel to Olderion and talk to Amelia near the Inn. Now go to Waterfall Way and find Amelia at the first stone bridge, two screens past the entrance. After the scene, return to the bulletin board at Zoldaad, and the quest will be done.

Charlotte is available as soon as you start Chapter 7. Go to Grandport Harbor and talk to her at the port to start The Shield of the Weak sub quest. Voyage to Grandshelt Castle and interact with the three markers before learning that your next destination is Kolobos Ruins.

From Kolobos Ruins' entrance, keep moving until you change screens and find three cloaked NPCs. A battle will ensue against a level 41 Magitek Weapon and three level 40 Former Knights. They're easy, so show them the power of the commanders of the Knights of Grandshelt.

Next stop: Cavern of Swords. It's the cave in the desert just northeast of Grandport Harbor, close to the Sanctum of Cloud. Enter to find a pretty conspicuous old lady in a rough, dusty cave. After talking to her, prepare for battle. You'll face a level 45 Magitek Weapon, not an elder supported by a cane, you monster! The Magitek is weak. Just employ Lightning and Water abilities.

Meet Charlotte back at Grandshelt Castle and that's it. Her knightly powers will accompany you as a Vision.

After you meet Ayaka for the first time in the main story, you can start her sub quest right away, still in the Town of Sian. The quest is The Admirable Apprentice, and it requires you to visit a bunch of dungeons past. The first is the Waterfall Way, so just go there and interact with the marker by the entrance.

Next is the Infernal Hollow in Zoldaad's Volcano. In it, you'll face a level 4 Ashasaur. It's weak against Light and Fire, so exorcise it with holy flames. Then, go to Mt. Thunderclap. From the entrance save point, teleport to the second one, and interact with a nearby tree. Now, return to Sian, talk to Ayaka one last time, and you finally have another Medic Vision in your arsenal.

In the ocean between the Grandshelt continent and Grandport Harbor, you can find a whirlpool. If you fly above it, you can enter this whirlpool to an area quite similar to a Sanctum.

When talking with the Will of the Crystal, though, you won't receive a new Vision on the spot. Instead, you'll have to battle for it, a battle against none other than Sephiroth. The boss is level 45 and quite challenging, as most optional bosses are in JRPGs, so you should be well prepared before trying to add him to your ranks.

Sephiroth is insanely tough, has a bunch of skills that can easily kill one person or your whole party in one go, and constantly changes tactics, so it's hard to pin down one party composition and go for it. Once you win, you'll get Sephiroth Vision and the Will Crystallized achievement/trophy for getting all Visions, in case he was your last.

articles.body:
During your adventures in Final Fantasy Resonance , you will find Adamantite, materials you can use to craft new weapons for your party members. You find the first one in Chapter 4, and you can get the rest in various ways, but you can only use them at the start of Chapter 6 after recruiting the Vision Aileen .

Where to Find Every Adamantite in Final Fantasy Resonance

We listed the location of every Adamantite in Final Fantasy Resonance in order of appearance. Some are rewards for collecting a specific number of Tablet Shards, so we recommend checking our Tablet Shards guide to not miss one as you progress through the main story of Final Fantasy Resonance.

Upon arriving in Zoldaad, the Imperial Capital during Chapter 4, you can check the notice board to learn that the Grandshelt Colosseum has reopened. The first challenge is the Fledgling League, which has a recommended level of 25. You earn your first Adamantite for winning Fledgling Battle 2 , which is level 27. The encounter is against a Chimera and is easily done if you are around the recommended level.

The second Adamantite lies at the start of Chapter 6, right after you unlock the treasure hunting radar. First, head over to Gaberada, the Undertown. Then, walk behind the inn to find a hidden staircase. Climb down and talk to an NPC who will hand you a Magi-tenna. Deliver the Magi-tenna to Lid on the Airship, and she will upgrade the radar, allowing you to hunt for treasures around the world.

This Adamantite is the very first treasure you can find using your Airship. It is located on the Olderion Federation continent , a bit south of the Aquapolis.

In the Gaberada pub, a few NPCs will mention a traveling Merchant Ship, one which you can find by cruising the world in your Airship. Once you interact with this Merchant Ship, you can buy an item from them. The first item this ship sells is yet another Adamantite for 35,000 Gil .

While the Merchant Ship is constantly on the move, we believe its spawn location stays the same in every playthrough. You can find this one near the Kingdom of Pharm, the continent on the west side of the map.

On your way to the Gronoa Shrine, you'll cross the Rugged Mountain Path. This Adamantite is inside a chest in the mountain , near the entrance. Really hard to miss.

Reward for delivering 80 Tablet Shards to the Princess at the Castle Oblivion. You get this many shards during the Rugged Mountain Path dungeon. If you need help finding them, use our Tablet Shard guide.

First-time reward for winning Brawler Battle 2 at the Colosseum . The battle is against two common elite enemies. Just do your thing and claim victory.

First-time reward for winning Brawler Battle 3 at the Colosseum . The Ochu boasts insane HP, but it takes pretty heavy damage whenever every Microchu is defeated, so focus on the minions.

Reward for delivering 89 Tablet Shards to the Princess at the Castle Oblivion. You get this many shards after concluding Mt. Reizan. If you need help finding them, use our Tablet Shard guide.

Aileen will start crafting Adamantite weapons for you on the Airship deck starting in Chapter 6. All you need to do is bring her Adamantite and choose a party member. Below is a table with all weapons to help you decide.

Reduces damage taken from physical and magic attacks by 20%.

Grants Hone Senses and Placidity for 5 turns at the start of battle.

Increases potency of healing magic by 20%.

Grants Overclock and allows the wielder to act first at the start of battle.

Grants Tactic: Fluid Warfare for 3 turns and allows the wielder to act first at the start of battle.

Raises luck level by 8 at the start of battle.

Restores 2% of max MP upon dealing damage with a standard attack.

Grants Concentrate for 3 turns and Sage's Eye for 4 turns at the start of battle.

Increases the duration of debuffs and status ailments inflicted by the wielder by 2 turns.

Once you craft the last weapon you'll earn the trophy/achievement The Weaponsmith .

articles.title: Blue N.O.V.A. Introduces its Own (Literal) Halo to the PvE Shooter Genre | IGN Preview
articles.summary: Built around a potentially brilliant mechanic that feels tailor-made for a PvE shooter, Blue N.O.V.A. has a ton of potential. But I left my hands-on demo and interview session with a few questions. Leaning into casual PvE shooting mechanics and a procedurally generated map gives it mass appeal and obvious replay potential. But I didn’t see some of what GungHo seemed, well, most gung ho about; namely, their investment in this game’s characters.
articles.body:
The demo I played was really early, for context.

The ring system is unique and organically encourages cooperation amongst players.

The team promises an awesome voice cast, though I didn’t get to hear it.

Built around a potentially brilliant mechanic that feels tailor-made for a PvE shooter, Blue N.O.V.A. has a ton of potential. But I left my hands-on demo and interview session with a few questions. Leaning into casual PvE shooting mechanics and a procedurally generated map gives it mass appeal and obvious replay potential. But I didn’t see some of what GungHo seemed, well, most gung ho about; namely, their investment in this game’s characters.

Set in a far-flung future where a rogue AI threatens what remains of humanity, thus propelling the people to new worlds, you're tasked with fighting the program and hopefully taking back a planet on the way. Not the most original setup, but at least it's topical!

That premise is meant to set up an iconic cast, which the developers seem really excited about. Beyond the high-profile Japanese voice actors they promise to recruit, the Tokyo-based publisher has also invested heavily in creating V-Tubers from the cast of Blue N.O.V.A. and even runs their social media channels in character. It's a lot for a game that doesn't seem close to coming out (it’s currently listed for 2027 without a precise date or window). From the inside looking out, it's hard to gauge these things against the chunk of game I played, because aside from a few 3D models, there wasn't much there. These public personas were not represented in the slice I played.

Still, it's really early in development. Chances are, you won’t see it in the state I did; that’s not to dunk on it, but I missed out on a lot of the stuff that’s meant to bring these characters to life. I don’t generally judge a game like this on its voice acting above, say, its shooting mechanics, but I could feel its absence. Given the chance to charm or repel, I'd have more to say about these characters. Even from this far out, it’s difficult to overstate how invested GungHo is in bringing them to life.

Instead, my favorite thing about this demo is probably the most unique thing about this game. I don’t mean to blow smoke, but the Ring system is perfectly tuned to a co-op shooter, especially one that leans towards the casual audience. Any time you’re close enough to at least one other player (or as many as six), a visual ring will automatically form, centered on the highest-performing player among the group. That ring nets group bonuses, including unlimited ammo, which comes in handy for weapons with longer reload times, for example.

That AOE felt generous enough to accommodate six people, but not so forgiving that you’d get roped in from yards away. In other words, just right. I’ll admit I had some trouble keeping up with the group of developers helping me through my demo as I found my sea legs with Blue N.O.V.A.’s movement and stamina bar, but I figured it out eventually.

Taking advantage of that halo made fighting big bad bots a breeze, and removing the need to reload doubles down on the casual, spray-n-pray, easygoing pace of play. That’s rare for a shooter, though not necessarily my vibe. I chase the flow state killstreaks and white-knuckle shootouts in the middle of a battle royale storm. It’s why I play multiplayer shooters, so this was new for me.

The pace and structure, on the other hand, wasn’t new. From dropping onto an island to looting my downed enemies to meeting up with squadmates, this flow is as straightforward and approachable as it gets. Markers on your HUD help guide you where you want to go, which then naturally guides you into other players. This kind of flips the premise of a battle royale on its head, though the goal remains the same: find other players.

It didn’t take long for me to locate a crew of other players and start shooting down anything in our path. Once my ring of allies had taken down enough bots, picked up some good loot (dropped by our enemies), and explored a few tiles on the map, it was time to face off with the boss. We made our way to a gigantic, arena-shaped structure close to the middle of the map and took on a gigantic, dragon-like robot.

Like most of my experience, this boss fight was pretty easy. And without a lot of the things meant to breathe life and personality into Blue N.O.V.A., it’s hard to walk away with much of an impression beyond how much I liked the ring system. I played a handful of runs, all against the same boss, though GungHo promised they’d add more boss fights in the final game, which is slated for a 2027 release.

I’m really interested in what GungHo is doing here; the ring system, map size, and pace set up a satisfying, approachable loop for newcomers. But my demo with Blue N.O.V.A. seems like it’s not quite ready for primetime. Missing a lot of the special touches that are sure to make or break its longevity and sense of personality, I still have questions that only a more complete version of this game can realistically answer. Hopefully, the public playtest that starts next week will offer some more answers. If you’re interested in checking out this ring system and chill PvE loop out for yourself, you can register on Blue N.O.V.A.’s official site until October 29th.

articles.title: Rockstar Games Staff Set for 'Historic' Union Vote at the Same Time GTA 6 Comes Out
articles.summary: Rockstar Games staff will vote on union recognition amid the launch of GTA 6.
articles.body:
Rockstar staff will vote on union recognition amid the launch of GTA 6 .

Recognition of the IWGB Union at Rockstar will be put to an employee vote from November 12-26, which just so happens to coincide with the release of GTA 6 itself, on November 19.

The terms of the recognition deal were agreed following months of negotiations that took place even as the IWGB and Rockstar clashed over the firing of 31 workers for allegedly leaking company secrets in October last year. The IWGB has alleged the workers were unlawfully fired, and have accused Rockstar Games of union busting. The vote will overlap with the closing submissions of the ongoing employment tribunal, which are set for November 17-18.

Rockstar North and Take-Two Office Protest Photos Nov 2025

The deal would give workers a say over topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies, the IWGB said. Developer Rockstar North, which is part of GTA publisher Rockstar Games, is in Edinburgh, Scotland. If the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union wins the vote, it will become the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry, and, officials said, could boost unionisation efforts across the rest of the industry.

Throughout the process, Rockstar has indicated its willingness to work with staff on union recognition. Rockstar Head of Publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently told Bloomberg : “We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union.”

Rockstar North production co-ordinator and Rockstar Game Workers Union Committee Member Shanti Easton-Steel commented: “This November, we have the chance to make gaming history not once but twice. As all our hard work, skill and creativity are experienced by GTA 6 players for the first time, our voices will now be heard for the first time too.

“For me, this vote comes down to ensuring employees at Rockstar get honesty and openness surrounding the decisions that affect them. When management choices are kept hidden, we can’t properly address issues like the gender pay gap, the uneven and ever-changing policies on overtime pay, or the concerns many co-workers hold around job security post-release.

“This is our moment to secure a window onto the decisions that shape our lives, and a seat at the table to improve them. I’m immensely proud of the games Rockstar gives its fans — I want to be equally proud of the voice Rockstar gives its staff.”

Alex Marshall, President of the IWGB Union, called the vote “just as historic as the game release.”

“But for workers at Rockstar, it is so much more personal: it is fundamentally a choice about whether you get to have a say in how your day-to-day life is organised,” he continued.

“From pay and pensions to parental leave and overtime, this agreement is a real chance to be involved in decision-making at Rockstar by becoming part of a democratic and member-led union.”

Photo by Lesley Martin / AFP via Getty Images.

articles.title: Pocketpair Would Love to Release Palworld on Nintendo Switch 2, Despite Pokémon Legal Battle
articles.summary: The legal battle between Nintendo and Pocketpair is ongoing, but the Palworld developer hasn’t ruled out a Switch 2 version of its creature collecting survival game.
articles.body:
The legal battle between Nintendo and Pocketpair is ongoing, but the Palworld developer hasn’t ruled out a Switch 2 version of its creature collecting survival game.

Nintendo and The Pokémon Company are currently embroiled in ongoing litigation with Pocketpair in Japan, with patents that revolve around how Pokémon games work at the heart of the lawsuit. IP experts have indicated that Nintendo may only receive a $30,000 payout if it wins, but it's looking increasingly likely that Nintendo will lose.

Skirting around the elephant in the room in an interview with VGC , Pocketpair CEO Takuru Mizobe said he’d love to get Palworld on Switch 2. “Of course,” Mizobe replied when asked if the studio had Switch 2 ambitions. “First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry.

“It’s been an incredible platform. If there’s ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we’d love to have those conversations.”

Of course, the current legal dispute would have to play out before those conversations can happen, and that’s assuming there’s no bad blood once legal proceedings are done and dusted.

Nintendo filed a patent infringement lawsuit in September 2024, but the complaint was modified in November 2025 after Palworld updates changed some of the most egregious of the Pokemon-inspired game mechanics. One such mechanic was the ability to throw a sphere to summon a creature, which was removed in Early Access patch v0.3.11.

Now when you summon a Pal, it simply spawns directly beside your character while you hold out the sphere. This change to avoid stepping on Nintendo’s patent removed some of the tactical options the player had, since they were no longer able to summon a Pal to a specific spot to draw aggro or hit an enemy from a different angle.

The scope of the lawsuit is reduced, but Pocketpair versus Nintendo and The Pokémon Company remains an active case within the Tokyo District Court. A preliminary view — which is a first-impression assessment of a subject before all the facts are known or a final decision is made — is planned for November 9 this year.

Palworld hit its 1.0 release in July , netting close to 1 million concurrent players on Steam. In total, Palworld has reached over 40 million players .

articles.title: You Need to Have Completed Crimson Desert's Main Storyline to Begin Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane's New DLC Stories
articles.summary: You need to have completed Crimson Desert’s main storyline to begin Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane’s new DLC stories, Pearl Abyss has confirmed.
articles.body:
You need to have completed Crimson Desert’s main storyline to begin Kliff, Oongka, and Damiane’s new DLC stories, Pearl Abyss has confirmed.

Speaking on Dropped Frames , Pearl Abyss' Will Powers confirmed two entry points for the Charting the Unknown DLC, which launches on October 29. You’ll need to have completed the main storyline to play the first entry point, which is the epilogue story content for each of the three main characters. The second is, you need to have established the Greymane camp during Chapter 3 of the main game to be able to play the new open world content, which includes exploration, naval gameplay, and pretty much everything that is not the new character-specific story DLC.

“There's storylines for the three characters,” Powers explained. “Damiane, Oongka, and Kliff, you didn't really get to explore a lot of their backstory, a lot of their motivations during the main game. Now, it's effectively an epilogue for all three characters. What are they doing after? They're not necessarily together anymore and traveling together. After all of this, what is Oongka going to do in the world? What is Damiane going to do in the world? What is Kliff going to do in the world? So there are those storylines, which are really cool and unique in and of themselves.

“But then there's also this storyline and this quest line around this new area of the map that you can play though.”

Crimson Desert Enhanced: Charting the Unknown Screenshots

While completing the main Crimson Desert storyline is no mean feat (it’s a massive game that many are still soldiering through even now!), it makes sense that any epilogue story DLC would have to have this requirement rather than be baked into the main campaign to avoid spoilers.

Indeed, Powers made this point on the show. “It would ruin the story for people that are focused on that stuff,” he said. “If you want open world content, if you want to be able to access all that stuff, you can do it very early in the game. If you want story focused content, then you've probably already beaten the story. So you'll be able to continue along that.”

Still, it's worth noting that not that many have actually completed Crimson Desert's main story, in percentage terms at least. According to official Steam achievements data, just 10.8% of all players have unlocked the Expert Storyteller achievement, which is awarded for completing all main quests. Perhaps we shouldn't be surprised by the data here; Crimson Desert is a game packed with hundreds, if not thousands of hours of content, and it is easy to get sidetracked. Personally, I've logged nearly 70 hours in Crimson Desert on Steam, but am nowhere near finishing the main story. I'm not sure I ever will.

Charting the Unknown adds new stories, ocean exploration, romance, business management and expanded housing to an already feature-packed Pywel. We have everything you need to know about the major additions in a Crimson Desert Charting the Unknown DLC features roundup .

articles.title: Spending time with the Echo Time — a smart clock that senses you sleeping
articles.summary: Amazon’s $199.99 smart alarm clock has a 3.2-inch round display, hundreds of clockfaces, no camera, and ultrasound sleep sensing.
articles.body: Amazon just announced its newest smart alarm clock — the Echo Time. The baseball-sized smart speaker with a screen, the Time looks like an Echo Dot with Clock and an Echo Spot had a much bigger baby. It features a 3.2-inch touchscreen that prominently displays your choice of a huge selection of clockfaces and includes a sleep-sensing feature that promises to rouse you at just the right time in your sleep cycle to help you feel more rested. It costs $199.99 and is available to order now. I spent some time with the Time at Amazon’s event in New York City and was impressed by several upgrades over the Spot, one of my favorite smart alarm clocks. The biggest is that you can set an alarm using the touchscreen, so you won’t wake your partner when you try to set one with your voice late at night. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The Time’s screen is an upgrade over the Spot’s 2.83-inch version: It’s fully round, whereas the Spot uses a cramped semicircle, and it shows a much bigger clock, which improves glanceability across the room. The Time also prioritizes the clock at all times, so no matter what you ask Alexa to do — turn the lights on, play music, show you who’s at your video doorbell (on a very tiny screen) — it will revert to the clock as soon as the action is completed. If you’re playing music and have a timer running, small icons above the clock let you tap into them for more detail while keeping the clock visible. The Time’s screen can dim down to under 0.3 nits. I saw this demoed, and it was barely visible in a very bright room, which is impressive, but I’ll have to get it on my bedside table to really test it. [Media: Like the Spot, the Time has no camera, making it more suitable to put on your bedside table than an Echo Show. It does add an ultrasound transducer to the Dot’s ultrasound sensor, which detects motion. Combined, these enable a new smart alarm feature that uses the sensors to track your breathing and small movements to estimate your sleep stage, and wake you at an optimal moment up to an hour before your alarm goes off. Sleep sensing is opt-in, and you can quickly disable it by pressing the mute button. If you’re a serial snoozer, the Time has a selection of special alarm tones that start quietly and “build energy” every time you hit that snooze button (by tapping the top of the speaker or by telling Alexa to snooze), to help make waking up less painful. [Image: The Time in day mode (left) and night mode (right). Night mode removes all blue light and can dim to below 0.3 nits of brightness (dimmer than pictured) [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: If you don’t like waking up to loud noises, the Time has a sunrise wake-up feature that gradually brightens the clockface with warm colors to help you wake up. This seemed very subtle in the demo I saw, but the room was brightly lit. If the Time were right next to your face, I could see it being effective for light sleepers. The Time has the same hardware as the new Echo Dot, also announced this week, so it features a built-in smart home hub (Zigbee, Thread, and Matter), meaning you can pair smart lights in your room with it to brighten them along with the clockface. I’ve been using light to wake up for several years now and can’t imagine going back to a jarring alarm. [Image: Amazon went all out on clockface options with Time; there are hundreds to choose from, and you can customize them to your heart’s content. The Time also comes in pink, black, or white, and there are two jazzy kids’ editions in galactic grape and cosmic lime. [Image: The kids’ version shows animations as part of a Sleep Studio feature. These cost $209.99 and include a year of Amazon Kids Plus, which features a Sleep Studio that provides guided bedtime routines that prompt your kids to put on their PJs and brush their teeth. It also offers Wind Down prompts and can slowly dim the lights. The kids’ clockfaces feature cute animated characters, plus analog faces for kids learning to tell time. [Image: Some of the more playful clockfaces designed for kids. On paper, the Time fixes many of the Spot’s problems and feels like a more polished device — and at nearly twice the price, it should be. My main concern is its size; it feels a hair too large for a bedside clock, though it’s smaller than the popular Hatch Restore. That’s a big screen for the bedside — though not as big as your phone — and if it could replace that on your bedside table, I can see it being a useful gadget. An optional stand ($39.99) lets you adjust the screen angle and makes it feel less bulky, but I’ll have to test it in my bedroom before making a final verdict. Photos by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.title: Valve 'Thinking About How to Solve' Steam's AI Slop Problem, but Won't Limit Developer Access
articles.summary: Valve’s Steam Business Team took to the stage at the Steam Indie Connect event in Korea and took questions from an audience of game developers. During the chat, the issue of Steam being flooded with generative AI slop games and knockoff AI clones came up, and Valve said it’s still trying to figure out how to navigate this new world.
articles.body:
Valve’s Steam Business Team took to the stage at the Steam Indie Connect event in Korea and took questions from an audience of game developers. During the chat, the issue of Steam being flooded with generative AI slop games and knockoff AI clones came up, and Valve said it’s still trying to figure out how to navigate this new world.

Last year, roughly 17% of Steam Next Fest demos disclosed the use of generative AI, and this year was likely higher as the platform hosted over 8,000 demos during the event. It’s a huge discoverability problem for developers who’ve poured years of their lives into their games, only to get swept up in the slop deluge.

Then there are the AI clones , which are becoming a growing issue. Developers are becoming more and more concerned about showing off their games, as bad actors are using generative AI to clone them from early footage and demos, beating them to the market with a bad copy.

During Steam Indie Connect, Valve’s Tom Giardino addressed concerns around clones, noting that they existed before AI and have only accelerated the process. "We don't want to be gatekeepers telling developers which tools they should or shouldn't use," he said (thanks, InvaGlobal ), ruling out Valve outright banning developers who do this.

"Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective," he added, shifting the onus onto the developer of the original game.

The issue of discoverability also came up, with developers in the audience noting that it’s harder than ever to stand out among all the throwaway AI games flooding digital storefronts like Steam, but particularly during Next Fest where developers are looking to find their audience ahead of release. According to Valve’s Marc Wilkinson, it’s not as bad as it seems.

During the first two days of Next Fest, recommendations are completely random, but personalized recommendations kick in later based on user activity. Once that kicks in, players are more likely to find the games they love. Wilkinson said that articles pointing out the flood of low-quality games were based on the first couple of days, before personalized recommendations kicked in.

According to Valve, the algorithm has to be completely random at first. This is to prevent system abuse from developers figuring out how to game the algorithm.

"We recognize that the trade-off is that some low-quality games get exposed," Wilkinson said. "We are fully aware of the situation, and a significant number of people are thinking about how to solve this problem."

Giardino added, "We don't think we're perfect and there's plenty of room for improvement. Rather than limiting developer access, making Steam a smarter and more dynamic platform is the starting point of our philosophy."

articles.title: How Does LEGO PlayStation Compare to the Actual Console?
articles.summary: See LEGO PlayStation and Sony's original console side-by-side to see how the LEGO version stacks up to the real thing.
articles.body:
I’m a nostalgic gamer who likes building LEGO sets, which makes me the exact target audience for the LEGO PlayStation set released earlier this month. I built LEGO PlayStation (and enjoyed the whole process from start to finish), but it got me thinking. Since LEGO is billing this as a “near 1:1 scale” recreation of the original hardware, what if I dug out my old PlayStation and compared the two? So that’s exactly what I did.

It turns out, the LEGO designers really did make a near one-to-one recreation of the original hardware, at least on the outside (check out my interview with one of the designers ). The dimensions are almost identical on all sides of the machine. The LEGO version stands slightly taller than the original, but it’s not really noticeable unless you squat down to look at them from the side.

The front of the LEGO set is particularly impressive, with its memory card slots and controller ports. Just like with the real thing, you can plug the LEGO controller into the port on the LEGO console. The main difference is that the LEGO controller’s cord is shorter than the real thing – but that’s what you’d want in a non-functional display set, anyway.

Even the buttons on the console are similar. Pressing the Power button on the real PlayStation turns it on, illuminating a green light below the button. Pressing the same button on the LEGO version raises a translucent green LEGO piece into the same position where the light would be. The Open button is even more impressive. Pressing it on the original hardware opens the PlayStation’s lid so you can put in or remove a game disc. Pressing the same button on the LEGO set also opens the lid.

The main surface-level difference between the LEGO version of the PS1 and the real thing is the selection of ports on the back. The LEGO PlayStation lacks the red, white, and yellow RCA ports. I'm not sure why these were omitted – maybe there were no existing LEGO pieces that could suitably replicate them? But the LEGO set does have ports for Serial I/O, AV Multi Out, and AC In.

I no longer have the original PlayStation controller that came with my console. However, I still have a DualShock controller, which came out in 1997 and made controlling characters in 3D worlds much more intuitive than using a standard D-pad. The DualShock is roughly the same size as the original controller, but it features two analog sticks. The LEGO controller looks pretty similar, but is noticeably more blocky. Still, it’s a fine effort.

One of the biggest things that makes the LEGO PlayStation look similar to the original is that all of the logos and text that appear on the exterior of the console and controller are printed onto the LEGO pieces. They’re not stickers, which I would inevitably have put on slightly askew, making the whole thing look more amateurish. I’m glad they went that route.

As for the other differences? Opening the lid on the LEGO version doesn’t reveal a boring disc drive. It reveals miniature dioramas for 1997’s Gran Turismo and 1999’s Ape Escape. These are little self-contained worlds you can slide out of the set to display next to it, if you’d like. It’s a pretty cool little Easter egg for fans of those games.

LEGO PlayStation vs. the Original Console

Overall, I’m pretty blown away by how similar LEGO PlayStation is to the real thing. Turns out those LEGO designers really know what they’re doing.

articles.title: With The Division 3 Still in Active Development, Ubisoft Announces The Division Franchise Has Hit More Than 50 Million Players
articles.summary: Massive Entertainment has announced that The Division series has recorded over 50 million players across its games, just as the series hits its 10th anniversary. That’s a lot of +1 defense beanies!
articles.body:
Massive Entertainment has announced that The Division series has recorded over 50 million players across its games, just as the series hits its 10th anniversary. That’s a lot of +1 defense beanies!

The long-running looter shooter began life in 2016 with the launch of The Division. It came out three years after its flashy reveal at Ubisoft's E3 2013 conference which, at the time, exceeded expectation for next-gen gaming (remember when the guy closed the car door while in cover?). The Division 2 followed in 2019, but sales failed to meet Ubisoft's expectations. A number of spinoffs have come and gone since.

Massive Entertainment announced a new DLC for The Division 2 at a community panel at Gamescom earlier this year. The Echoes of Central Park DLC releases on November 3. It seems likely the new expansion — which adds a horror-themed flashback campaign, a stash space increase, a level boost, and more — will see even more players shoot numbers out of some guys across the U.S., both returning and new.

With those kinds of numbers, it’s no surprise Ubisoft and Massive aren’t done with the series. Tom Clancy's The Division 3 is also officially in production at Massive Entertainment. Originally headed up by executive producer Julian Gerighty (who also led Star Wars Outlaws and The Division 2), The Division 3 is now in the hands of creative director Mathias Karlson, game director on The Division 2. Gerighty recently left Ubisoft to work at Battlefield developer DICE .

Gerighty confirmed his departure in a social media post just a week after appearing on a livestream to promote The Division 3 . “So, The Division 3 is in production, right?” he said before his departure. “This is not a secret. It's been announced. It's shaping up to be a monster.

“I can't really say anything more than that. But this is, within these walls in Massive, we are working extremely hard on something that I think will be as big an impact as Division 1 was.”

Tom Clancy’s The Division 2 Echoes of Central Park DLC Screenshots

Following his departure, Massive reassured fans that The Division 3 was in safe hands. “For our players, don’t worry, Agents,” the studio said in a social media post. “Our teams who built this world with Julian are still here, carrying it forward with an ambitious, unchanged commitment to the future.”

There’s no word on when The Division 3 will launch, but Ubisoft is making it a priority. Late last year, Massive Entertainment introduced what it called a "voluntary career transition program," as part of a move to focus on The Division franchise and its Snowdrop game engine.
